display.purpose: First-run card headline. The only type above 15px in the product.

brand.purpose: The Shotframe wordmark in the command bar.

body.purpose: Base interface size; hints and paragraph copy derive from it.

control.purpose: Segmented buttons, chips, small buttons, phone tab labels.

label.purpose: Group headings, menu labels, preset and motion captions.

numeral.purpose: Every value a user reads: dimensions, durations, percentages, keycaps, export meta. Always tabular.

shadows.name: lift-1
shadows.purpose: Small objects resting on a slab, e.g. the brand mark.

shadows.name: lift-2
shadows.purpose: Transient objects a short distance off the surface: sample badge, drop-hint pill, hovered preset swatch.

shadows.name: lift-3
shadows.purpose: Every glass slab and the toast. The room's default float height.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: The canvas plate only: deepest cast in the room plus a one-pixel light ring.

shadows.name: slab-inner-light
shadows.purpose: Paired with lift-3 on every slab; reads as light falling from above.

shadows.name: primary-button-light
shadows.purpose: The export button alone: lit top face and amber cast into the room.

shadows.name: selected-ring
shadows.purpose: Selected swatch, wallpaper or ink dot: a dark gap then an amber ring.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default curve for colour, bed and atmosphere changes.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Hover and state colour transitions on controls.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The damped release. Control presses and slab entrances decelerate into rest and never bounce.

motion.name: relight
motion.purpose: Glow-dependent properties (slab tint, lit top edge, ambient and plate halo) when the sampled palette changes.

motion.name: slab-down
motion.purpose: Command bar entrance from the top edge.

motion.name: slab-right
motion.purpose: Inspector entrance from the right edge.

motion.name: slab-up
motion.purpose: Toolbar entrance from the bottom edge.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Transient surfaces only: menu, tool options, toast, sample badge, first-run card.

motion.name: tab-in
motion.purpose: Replays the inspector body on tab change.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active-state compression on buttons and tools; released on --settle.

narrative.overview:
Shotframe is a near-black room with the lights off and one object lit: the user's screenshot on its plate at the centre. Everything else in the room is smoked glass floating above that darkness — a command bar along the top, an inspector down the right, a tool bar at the bottom of the stage. Nothing is docked into a chrome frame, nothing is divided by a structural border; the slabs read as separate objects because light falls on their top edge and darkness pools between them.

The room takes its colour from the work. When an image loads, palette() samples it and publishes two hues onto --glow-a and --glow-b; those feed the ambient wash behind the plate, the glow the plate throws, the tint mixed into every glass slab, and the lit top edge that separates each slab from the dark. The interface is therefore never a fixed colour scheme — it is a room lit by the object in it, and it re-lights over 700ms whenever the object changes.

Density is high and quiet. Controls are small (34px tall, 13px base type), labels are always written out rather than left to icons, and every numeral is monospaced and tabular so a value never jitters while it is being dragged. The one saturated colour in the chrome is amber; it marks state and nothing else. This world explicitly refuses the docked-toolbar-plus-settings-form arrangement that every other screenshot tool ships.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black room (#08070a) with floating smoked-glass slabs, never a docked chrome frame
Separation by light and darkness, not by structural borders
One amber accent, used only to mark state
Ambient light sampled at runtime from the user's own image
Archivo throughout, Spline Sans Mono for every numeral
Damped physical motion: decelerate into place, never bounce

rules.name: The One Lit Object Rule
rules.body: The screenshot plate is the brightest thing on screen. No chrome surface may out-glow it; slabs stay at glass values and only the plate carries a halo.

rules.name: The Borrowed Light Rule
rules.body: Room colour is never authored per-surface. Anything that should feel lit reads --glow-a / --glow-b, which the image publishes at runtime. A new surface that wants warmth mixes the glow token in; it does not pick a hue.

rules.name: The Amber-Is-State Rule
rules.body: Amber means "this is on, focused, selected or about to export". Never use it for emphasis, decoration or hierarchy.

rules.name: The Dim-Is-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: --dim never carries a glyph. Text bottoms out at --faint.

rules.name: The Numerals-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any digit a user reads as a value — dimensions, times, percentages, scale factors, keycaps — is set in Spline Sans Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Digits inside prose stay in Archivo.

rules.name: The Say-What-It-Is Rule
rules.body: Every control that can carry a word carries one. Inspector tabs ship an icon and a written label; tools carry an aria-label and a title with the shortcut. An icon alone makes people guess, and this world does not make people guess.

rules.name: The Two-Faces Rule
rules.body: Archivo and Spline Sans Mono are the complete type inventory. No third family, and no system-UI display face.

rules.name: The Anchored-To-The-Work Rule
rules.body: On phone, stacked surfaces position against --plate-h, the canvas's measured height, not against a guessed constant. Any new stacked surface reads the same variable.

rules.name: The Room-Margin Rule
rules.body: Floating surfaces sit 14px from the room's edges. 16px for the bottom of the two lower slabs. Nothing touches the wall.

rules.name: The Light-Not-Borders Rule
rules.body: Separation is achieved with a lit top edge (color-mix(--glow-a 38%, --edge-lit)), an inner highlight and shadow. A full-strength border on all four sides is not how this world separates things.

rules.name: The No-Hard-Offset Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is soft, negative-spread and near-black. No hard offset shadow, no coloured glow except the amber cast under the export button and the blurred image-sampled ambience.

rules.name: The Radius-By-Role Rule
rules.body: A new surface takes the radius of its role — slab 16, plate 12, control 9, tool 10, chip 8 — not a value picked to suit its size.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: Motion decelerates into rest and never overshoots. A bounce, a spring or an elastic curve is out of this world.

rules.name: The Entrance-From-Edge Rule
rules.body: A slab enters from the edge it lives on, with a stagger. Nothing fades in from nowhere.

dos: Do build any new floating surface as a .slab: glass fill with the glow mixed into its top, 20px backdrop blur, Lift 3, lit top border, 16px radius.
Do read --glow-a / --glow-b for anything that should look lit, so the surface re-lights with the user's image.
Do set every value, dimension, duration and keycap in Spline Sans Mono with tabular numerals.
Do give every control a written label, an aria-label, or both; tabs carry icon and word together.
Do keep amber for state — on, focused, selected, exporting.
Do take radius from role (slab 16px, plate 12px, control 9px, tool 10px, chip 8px).
Do press controls with the damped --settle release and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do draw icons as inline SVG stroke paths on the 24-unit grid.
donts: Don't separate two surfaces with a full-strength four-sided border; separate them with a lit top edge, an inner highlight and shadow.
Don't let any chrome surface out-glow the canvas plate.
Don't use --dim on text; --faint is the floor.
Don't use amber for emphasis, decoration or hierarchy.
Don't introduce a third type family or a system-UI display face into the chrome.
Don't add a hard offset shadow or a coloured glow beyond the export button's amber cast and the image-sampled ambience.
Don't ship an icon-only control without a label or accessible name.
Don't use a bouncing, springing or elastic curve.
Don't dock chrome into a solid frame or wrap settings in a form panel with structural rules — that is the arrangement this world exists to refuse.

acceptedDeviations.name: Full-bleed command bar
acceptedDeviations.body: The direction contract's FIRST VIEWPORT describes a glass command bar floating at top centre. The build ships .bar at left: 14px; right: 14px — a full-width slab respecting the room margin. Deliberate adaptation: the bar carries the wordmark, Open and Paste, the Static/Motion switch, undo and redo, Copy, and the Export split button with its meta string, and a centred pill cannot hold that payload at 1440px without crowding. Every other property of the world is kept, and the Static/Motion switch is absolutely centred within the bar so the contract's centred focal point survives inside a full-bleed container.
